arguments.value: Judith Morgenstern Barzilay (born 1944) is a senior judge of the U.S. Court of International Trade, taking the bench in 1998 after nomination by President Bill Clinton and assuming senior status in 2011. A native of Russell, Kansas, she earned a B.A. from Wichita State University, an M.L.S. from Rutgers University, and a J.D. from Rutgers School of Law–Newark. Before entering the judiciary, Barzilay worked as a high school teacher and librarian, served as a law clerk in New Jersey, practiced privately, and held positions as a trial attorney in the U.S. Department of Justice and in private practice in New York City. She later spent a decade at Sony Electronics, where she served in senior legal and executive roles in import-export operations and government affairs, and she also served on the Treasury Advisory Committee on Commercial Operations of the U.S. Customs Service.
